title: Chapter 72
content:
Stepping out of the sedan with Secretary Yoon in tow, Seok-joo carried the wooden box of herbal tonics up the front steps of Kang Il-hyun’s private estate.

It was his first visit in nearly a full year. Back when Jang Yi-an was around, he had dropped by frequently, but ever since the guy vanished, Seok-joo had steered clear. The security perimeter remained as impenetrable as ever, with massive, trained patrol hounds prowling the cleared lawn.

The moment he stepped into the foyer, the senior housekeeper came forward to greet him.

"Welcome, Young Master."

Her smile was warm and practiced. Seok-joo offered a stiff, superficial nod. If there was anyone under this roof who unnerved him as much as Kang Il-hyun, it was this old woman. Always wearing that same pleasant, grandfatherly mask—a smile so fixed and unreadable it felt like staring at a framed portrait. It was quietly terrifying.

Taking the wooden chest from Secretary Yoon, Seok-joo held it out.

"Father sent this over for my brother. Said it’s a restorative tonic for the midsummer heat."

"Oh, my word... what a precious gift. I will be sure to present it to President Kang the moment he returns."

"Where... did my brother go?"

"He stepped out on business early this morning. I don't expect him back until late tonight."

"Ah. Right."

"Would you care to wait inside for him, Young Master?"

Seok-joo shook his head in immediate, violent refusal. His only assignment was to confirm whether Kang Il-hyun was physically at home and drop off the delivery.

Declining her offer of iced tea, he turned to leave when low, masculine voices drifted from the second-floor mezzanine. He glanced toward the staircase, but the landing was empty. Curious, he turned back to the housekeeper.

"Do we have guests staying over?"

"Yes, sir. Several gentlemen will be lodging with us for the time being."

Assuming they were corporate fixers, Seok-joo put it out of his mind and headed for the doors. His sole priority was clearing out before his second brother unexpectedly walked through the gate and subjected him to another round of verbal abuse.

Politely waving the housekeeper back inside, he walked down the paved drive toward the security gate, pausing when hushed murmurs caught his ear from the smoking nook behind the garage.

He signaled for Secretary Yoon to wait by the car and slipped closer behind the hedges.

Two security guards were taking a drag. At first, it sounded like idle small talk about the suffocating summer heat, and Seok-joo was about to turn away when a familiar title caught his attention.

"When is President Kang coming back?"

"Who knows? He'll probably be holed up out there for a while."

Seok-joo held his breath, leaning in closer. The housekeeper just said he was returning tonight.

"He didn't head out alone, did he?"

"Beats me."

"Assistant Manager Kim mentioned he saw that Hong Kong guy in the back of the transport. Said the guy looked like a corpse."

"Get out of here. The brothers are walking around upstairs completely fine."

"I'm dead serious. Kim swore he saw him with his own eyes."

"That's crazy..."

Hearing footsteps approaching the gravel, Seok-joo broke into a hurried, silent jog toward the main gate.

He slipped into the rear of the waiting sedan as Secretary Yoon engaged the ignition. Sinking into the leather, Seok-joo turned the guards' conversation over in his head.

A Hong Kong guy?

Without warning, the striking, handsome face of Jang Yi-an—the guy he had randomly bumped into at the Gangnam club days ago—flashed through his mind.

No... come on. That's impossible.
Consciousness felt like a boulder chained to his chest, dragging him down into dark, murky water.

Jakyeong fought through the haze, forcing his heavy lids apart. Bit by bit, soft morning sunlight began bleeding through the sheer curtains, illuminating the room.

He lifted a trembling arm, inspecting his raw wrists.

The dark purple chafing from the leather restraints was undeniable. Across his ribs and thighs, dull aches flared from the shrapnel bruises and scratches sustained during the island explosion.

Relief that he was still breathing washed over him, followed immediately by an urgent instinct: I need to get the fuck out of here.

He swung his legs over the edge of the mattress, but the lingering chemical sedative turned his knees to rubber.

His soles hit the hardwood, buckled, and sent him sprawling. He dragged himself up, gripping the nightstand, and stumbled along the wall.

Scanning the suite, he realized the architecture was completely foreign. Where the hell am I?

Searching for an exit, his eyes snagged on a figure standing motionless in the dim alcove near the wardrobe.

A choked gasp caught in his throat.

Standing in the corner was an identical, life-sized replica of himself.

Jakyeong froze, blinking in disoriented horror. Did I actually die? Am I staring at my own dead corpse? Is this another paralytic nightmare?

He slapped his own cheeks hard, pinching his forearm until it bruised. The sharp sting was unmistakably real.

Approaching on trembling legs, he reached out to touch the figure. The skin was synthetic silicone—a painstakingly sculpted, full-body anatomical mannequin cast in his exact likeness.

Horrified, Jakyeong cautiously hooked a finger into the mannequin's briefs. Even his cock had been molded into uncanny, lifelike detail.

Jakyeong recoiled in pure revulsion. When the fuck did that lunatic have this fabricated?!

Bolting through the bedroom doors, he found himself in an expansive, sun-drenched open-concept villa. Faint metallic clatter and running water drifted from the gourmet kitchen down the hall.

Peering around the corner, a broad, tailored back came into view.

Standing before the marble prep island was Kang Il-hyun, muttering soft, frustrated curses under his breath as he wrestled with the cookware.

A sudden wave of vertigo made Jakyeong sway, his palm slapping hard against a dining chair for balance.

The noise broke the silence. Il-hyun spun around—a heavy chef's knife gripped in his right hand, his eyes bloodshot and blazing with a furious, unhinged intensity that looked ready to butcher whatever moved.

"S-Stay back..." Jakyeong stammered, raising a weak, defensive arm as he took a ragged step backward.

Il-hyun strode forward, chef's knife in hand.

Instead of raising the blade, he smoothly slid a dining chair back, caught Jakyeong’s shoulders with his free hand, and gently guided him into the seat. Jakyeong couldn't tear his terrified gaze from the kitchen knife resting inches from his chest.

Setting the blade on the table, Il-hyun slipped a soft linen cushion behind Jakyeong’s aching lower back, leaned in, and planted a sweet, lingering kiss on his cheek.

"Sleep well, darling?"

The gentle greeting left Jakyeong utterly speechless. The bloodthirsty monster who had hovered over the operating slab was nowhere to be found. Drained by the lingering paralytic, Jakyeong didn't even have the physical strength to throw a punch.

Il-hyun placed a steaming mug of herbal tea before him, pulling out the opposite chair and settling down with his chin resting on his knuckles.

A dazzling, serene smile spread across his face.

"So tell me... how does it feel to return from the dead?"

Jakyeong gripped the warm ceramic, glaring across the table with raw venom. I should crack this mug over your skull right now.

"Where the hell are we?"

"We'll be staying here for a while," Il-hyun purred smoothly. "Since you seemed so desperately starved for my attention, I decided to keep you by my side twenty-four hours a day. I plan to shower you with absolute, overflowing affection."

The sheer, sadistic euphoria radiating from the man when he emphasized overflowing affection sent a violent shiver down Jakyeong's spine. His brow twitched in sheer disbelief.

"Look at you," Il-hyun teased. "Practically trembling with joy."

"Stop playing games," Jakyeong rasped. "Where are Han-ge and Ryun-ge?"

"Safe and sound. I wanted to turn them both into fertilizer, but since I didn't want my darling to hate me forever, I spared their lives. Aren't I an angel?"

Seeing the obvious skepticism in Jakyeong's eyes, Il-hyun dialed a video feed on his burner.

Park Tae-soo's stone-faced profile appeared on screen, promptly panning the camera to Wang Han and Wang Ryun. Aside from superficial scratches and bandages, both brothers looked intact and well-fed.

Noticing Il-hyun on the line, Ryun immediately launched into shameless, sycophantic flattery:

[President Kang, our deepest apologies! We should have filed for formal leave before heading on vacation, it completely slipped our minds! Surely there are no lingering misunderstandings, right? Please take wonderful care of our dear Jakyeong! Such unmatched generosity, such breathtaking visuals, and a truly magnificent character to match—we are in absolute awe! Haha!]

Fearing Ryun would elevate the sociopath to literal sainthood if left unchecked, Jakyeong reached over and severed the call.

At least they were breathing.

He slid the phone back across the marble, meeting Il-hyun’s amused gaze.

"Care for some music?" Il-hyun asked cheerfully.

Before Jakyeong could reply, Il-hyun aimed a sleek remote toward the integrated surround-sound system.

The speakers initialized, and Jakyeong’s own panicked, desperate screams from the taxidermy lab erupted through the villa at maximum volume:

[President Kang, I like you!]

Jakyeong’s face twisted into an expression of pure, agonizing mortification.

[I really like you! Running away was a stupid mistake! I spent every day agonizing over whether I should come back to you! I've never experienced such sublime, incredible sex in my entire life! Please, believe me!]

You sick, sadistic son of a bitch.

Jakyeong lunged across the table to snatch the remote, but Il-hyun casually leaned back, holding the device behind his spine with a wicked, triumphant laugh. Jakyeong scrambled around the island, attempting to wrestle it away, but the audio loop continued blasting through the ceiling speakers on an infinite, concussive cycle.

In his weakened state, overpoweringly outmatched, Jakyeong couldn't gain an inch.

Il-hyun caught both of Jakyeong's wrists in one large hand, hoisted the boy cleanly over his shoulder in a fireman's carry, and strode toward the living room.

Tossing Jakyeong onto the plush sectional, Il-hyun pinned the boy's flailing shoulders down with one hand while tapping the remote with the other.

The floor-to-ceiling motorized blinds rolled upward, revealing a panoramic, unobstructed view of the glittering turquoise sea.

The breathtaking coastal horizon froze Jakyeong in place.

"Enjoy the view," Il-hyun said softly, letting go of the hold. "It might not be the exact property you were hunting for, but an island is an island."

Finding the boy quiet, Il-hyun dropped onto one knee before the sofa, bringing his eyes level with Jakyeong's. The lethal madness from yesterday had vanished entirely, replaced by a gaze so strikingly warm and gentle it was disorienting.

Through the speakers overhead, Jakyeong’s recorded voice continued to blare: [President Kang, I like you! Such sublime, incredible sex!]

"President Kang... I'm begging you. Turn that goddamn thing off."

"Only if you give me an honest answer."

"To what?!"

"While you were playing fugitive... how many times did I cross your mind?"

Jakyeong clamped his jaw shut.

At least once a day. Or was it dozens?

Refusing to give the bastard the satisfaction, he stared down at his knees. Yet the relentless recording continued to drill into his skull like psychological warfare.

Il-hyun leaned in closer. "Not even once?"

Jakyeong swallowed, his throat dry. Admitting defeat felt marginally better than enduring another hour of his own recorded confessions.

"I thought of you..." Jakyeong muttered under his breath.

A brilliant, breathtaking smile broke across Kang Il-hyun’s handsome face.

Jakyeong braced for a barrage of relentless, mocking follow-up questions, but Il-hyun simply pushed himself to his feet, looking thoroughly and completely satisfied.

"Good enough for me."

Before Jakyeong could process the relief, Il-hyun leaned down, planting a soft, sweet peck on his lips before pulling away.

Jakyeong’s brow pinched into an indignant scowl, aggressively rubbing the back of his hand across his mouth as he turned his face away. Yet beneath the irritation, his ears burned a fierce, undeniable crimson, and a strange, restless flutter stirred deep in his gut.

Whistling a jaunty tune, Il-hyun sauntered back into the kitchen, picked up the heavy chef's knife, and resumed furiously hacking away at the cutting board.

A moment later, he threw his head back toward the ceiling with a theatrical wince, his eyes streaming with tears as he hissed out a string of foul curses:

"Fuck me... these goddamn onions are lethal."

Jakyeong stared from the sofa in dead silence, only now realizing what the corporate heir had been crying over all morning.
